title and abstract.summary: This study quantified body size variation in the species Halictus ligatus across three different urban environments and compared the variation found in bees residing in each city. The study measured body size variation, specifically head width and intertegular distance, in female Halictus ligatus across three different Midwestern United States cities to determine if urban environments and temperature influenced these measurements.

introduction.summary: The study quantified and compared body size variation in the facultatively eusocial sweat bee species, Halictus ligatus, across three distinct Midwestern cities to determine if patterns of body size variation were conserved across urban landscapes or diverged among cities. This study measured the body size variation in the sweat bee Halictus ligatus across three different cities in the Midwestern United States (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis), and investigated how climate factors might influence this variation. methods.summary: The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of 240 Hylaeus ligatus females collected from community gardens in three Midwestern United States cities. The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of female Hylaeus ligatus to assess their relationship with overall body size and to compare these measurements across three different urban populations (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis) based on climatic data.

results.summary: The study measured the variation in body size of Halictus ligatus females collected across three Midwestern cities (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis) between May and October of 2016, finding significant differences in this variation among the cities. The study measured the variation in head width of H. ligatus bees across three surveyed cities (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis) and determined whether climatic variation in each city influenced this head width range. discussion.summary: The study measured the body size variation in the social sweat bee, Halictus ligatus, across three geographically separated urban cities: Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis. The study compared the body size variation of Halictus ligatus bees across three distinct urban systems to assess the role of seasonality and temperature on this variation.
